caption:
7 deductions that sound made up (but are legal). Save this for tax time.

1. Sunscreen: if your job has you outdoors for long periods.
2. Sunglasses and a hat: same condition. Used privately too? Only the work share.
3. Your tax agent's fee: the cost of managing your tax affairs, claimed in the following year's return.
4. Washing your uniform: the ATO accepts $1 a load (50c if it's mixed with other clothes). It has to be a real uniform, occupation-specific or protective clothing. Plain black pants and suits don't count.
5. Union and professional membership fees.
6. Income protection insurance premiums you pay yourself.
7. Donations of $2 or more to a registered charity (a DGR), when you get nothing in return. Raffle tickets don't count.

Numbers 3, 5, 6 and 7 sit on top of the new $1,000 standard deduction (2026–27). Work costs like 1, 2 and 4 count against it. Keep records for all of them.

Which one did you not know about?

#taxdeductions #taxreturn #australiantax #paylesslegally #moneytips
figures_checked: Sunscreen, sunhats and sunglasses claimable if required to work outdoors for prolonged periods; apportion private use (ATO Protective items, equipment and products, checked 15 Nov 2026)

Laundry reasonable basis $1 per load work clothes only, 50c mixed; conventional clothing not claimable; occupation-specific, protective, compulsory or registered uniforms only (ATO Clothing, laundry and dry-cleaning expenses, checked 15 Nov 2026)

Registered tax agent fee deductible as cost of managing tax affairs; donations of $2 or more to a DGR with no benefit in return (ATO Deductions for donations, investments and managing your tax affairs, checked 15 Nov 2026)

Standard deduction up to $1,000 from 2026–27, automatic, residents with labour income, no records; actual work claims reduce it; $300 work-expense and $150 laundry no-receipt exceptions end 1 July 2026; union fees, donations, tax agent fees, income protection premiums, personal super contributions, investment/rental deductions claimable on top (ATO Standard deduction for work-related expenses, updated 2 Nov 2026, checked 15 Nov 2026)
